Oct 22, 2026

Cloudflare MCP servers no longer serve /sse

Agents

Cloudflare's product-specific MCP servers now serve only /mcp. A request to /sse returns 410 Gone with the server's /mcp URL, which most MCP clients show in their connection error.

If your MCP client is configured with an /sse URL, change it to /mcp, for example https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. If you signed in through /sse, your client asks you to sign in again. Connections that already use /mcp are not affected.

Oct 22, 2026

Agents SDK now supports the latest Pi 1.4 release

Agents

Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4 ↗︎, and makes it recover more reliably from evictions, crashes, and storage errors.

  • Hibernation while Pi's tasks sleep. PiHarness passes Pi's new onWake callback to your harness factory. While a task sleeps, such as during a model retry backoff, the Durable Object can hibernate until the task is due instead of staying in memory.
  • Parked tasks. Pi 1.4 parks a task that keeps crashing the object instead of restarting it forever. Parked operations show as parked in pending(), and session.retry() runs them again.
  • Recovery from storage errors. PiHarness reopens Pi after a storage error instead of failing every call until the object restarts. Its wake-up job retries failed steps with a backoff instead of being dropped.
  • Retried model streams. agents/models/pi-ai reports a cut-off or idle model stream as a transient error, so Pi retries the turn instead of failing it.

Upgrade

The Agents SDK v0.30.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Pi 1.4 migrates the session storage in the object's SQLite database to a schema that Pi 1.3 cannot open, so a deployment cannot roll back past this upgrade. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.4.0 changelog ↗︎ for Pi's own breaking changes.

Oct 22, 2026

Sandbox SDK 0.12.14 updates trusted certificates after the eMudhra compromise

Sandboxes

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. Sandbox SDK images before 0.12.14 trust these certificates. An HTTPS connection that leaves the container directly, such as one from mountBucket(), backups, gitCheckout(), tunnels, or code that runs in the sandbox, can be intercepted with a forged certificate.

What you need to do

Sandbox SDK 0.x

Update immediately. Install @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.14, change the FROM line in your Dockerfile to the matching image, and redeploy. Keep any -python, -opencode, or -musl suffix on the image tag. The deployment's rollout replaces running sandboxes with ones that use the new image.

If you use the next prerelease, update to 0.13.0-next.825.1 or later.

If you cannot update yet and use 0.8.7 or later, send all HTTPS through your Worker, so that Cloudflare checks every certificate on port 443 whatever your image trusts:

Deploy, then stop running sandboxes so that they restart with the interception certificate. This does not cover TLS on other ports, such as cloudflared tunnels, and clients that ignore the injected certificate fail to connect. For more information, refer to HTTPS traffic.

Sandbox SDK 1.x

You do not need to update the SDK, because it makes no TLS connections of its own. Your image decides which certificates your sandboxes trust, so rebuild it and replace the sandboxes that run the old one:

  1. Run docker pull for each base image in your Dockerfile, then clear the Docker build cache with docker builder prune --all. wrangler deploy builds with your local images and build cache, so without these steps it can ship the old CA certificates and runtimes. If your Wrangler configuration references an image by digest, build and push a new image and update the digest instead.
  2. Deploy your Worker.
  3. Stop sandboxes that are still running, for example with this.ctx.container.destroy(). A running sandbox keeps the image it started with until it stops. To restart only the sandboxes whose image is out of date, refer to Roll out a named image update.
  4. If you use snapshots, create new ones from sandboxes that run the updated image. A snapshot restores the image it was created from, so an older snapshot brings back the old certificates.

Check your sandboxes

From inside a sandbox, connect to one of the test hosts listed at emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com ↗︎ with each TLS client your code uses, such as curl, node, or bun. Every request should fail:

What changed in 0.12.13 and 0.12.14

In the 0.12.13 images, the system CA bundle, Node.js, cloudflared, and pip reject certificates from the compromised intermediates. The images ship updated Ubuntu and Alpine CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4, cloudflared 2026.10.2, and pip 26.2.2 in the -python image.

0.12.14 updates Bun to 1.4.4, so the bun command and createBackup() uploads of archives of 10 MiB or more reject these certificates too. The -opencode image ships OpenCode 1.19.4 or later, which also runs on Bun 1.4.4.

Oct 21, 2026

createAI replaces workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider

AgentsWorkers AIAI Gateway

The Agents SDK has a new createAI function for the AI SDK and Pi AI. It unifies what workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider did: Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models, through the AI binding or an account id and API token.

workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now feature frozen and marked as deprecated. Please migrate at your convenience.

With createAI you get:

  • Every model by id. Workers AI @cf/ ids, any model in the AI Gateway catalog, and dynamic routes as dynamic/<route>.
  • Vendor model objects. Pass a model from the vendor's own package, such as ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")). It goes unchanged to AI Gateway's provider-native endpoint.
  • The binding, or an account id and API token. Use a gateway in another account, or call from outside a Worker.
  • Gateway options, fallback, and BYOK. Caching, logging, metadata, retries, byokAlias, zdr, and vendorKey.
  • Stream resume. Through the binding, a catalog or dynamic route stream that drops mid-answer resumes.
  • Other model types. Embeddings, images, speech, transcription, and reranking in the AI SDK provider, and images in Pi AI.
Before After
createWorkersAI({ binding }) createAI({ binding })
createWorkersAI({ accountId, apiKey }) createAI({ accountId, apiToken })
createAiGateway(...) createAI(...), with fallback for a list of models
createAISearch from workers-ai-provider createAISearchNamespace from ai-search-provider

For AI Search, use ai-search-provider. For more information, refer to Models.

Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization

Agents

The Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization ↗︎.

Grant only the required scopes when you connect, then authorize more on demand as your agent performs a task. When a tool call needs a scope you have not granted, the server returns an insufficient_scope challenge ↗︎ naming it, and your MCP client asks you to approve it. Scopes you already granted are kept.

To start with the least access, choose Minimal on the consent page when you connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Refer to authorization in MCP.

Available now in all MCP clients that support step-up authorization.

Oct 19, 2026

Introducing Clairic: an extraction model for typed values, now on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/cloudflare/clairic is now available on Workers AI as a preview. Clairic is the first extraction model: a System One model that answers with values instead of text. We intend to release the model with open weights soon.

Decision models such as Clef choose among options you define up front. Many structured-output tasks do not have answers you can list in advance: an invoice total, a delivery date, the number of days a shipment is late, or what a repair will cost. Clairic handles these. You send a state and a schema of typed fields, and it returns one typed value per field. A value is read from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it.

Clairic does not generate tokens. It reads your input in one pass and decodes each answer under the rules of its type, so every answer is a valid value of the type you asked for, or null when the input does not determine it.

Typed fields

Define as many fields as you need. Fields that do not fit beside the input in one pass are split across parallel passes, so there is no upper limit.

Type Returns
text An exact span of the input, with its character offsets
number A number read or worked out from the input, honoring integer and decimals
date, time, datetime Real calendar dates and valid times, in ISO form
duration A length of time in the unit you choose
list Every matching text, number, or date, in input order
estimate A distribution inside your min and max, on your step grid, on a linear or log scale
forecast One estimate per future step of a series, up to 64 steps

Every scalar answer includes p_null, the probability that the input does not determine the value, and a confidence score. Estimates and forecasts include a median and an 80% interval (p10 to p90). Set options.include_quantiles to also get all 99 percentiles. Use these to decide what to automate and what to send to review.

You can also pass up to four images alongside the state.

Preview

The current endpoint is an early checkpoint, and we expect it to improve:

  • Arithmetic: One- and two-step calculations, such as totals, differences, conversions, and date arithmetic, are reliable. Long chains of dependent steps and aggregations across many table rows are not yet. Extract the inputs with Clairic and do the math in code.
  • Estimates: Clairic estimates best when the input contains evidence such as comparables, history, or descriptive text. Without evidence, the interval is wide.
  • Forecasts: Forecasting is basic. Next-step forecasts follow recent patterns, but forecasts several steps out flatten toward the average, and Clairic does not anticipate events the series does not show, such as holidays. It does not replace a time-series model trained on your data.
  • Calibration: Intervals are trained to be calibrated and are on most held-out sets, but they can run narrow on unfamiliar data.
  • Confidence: Every answer is well formed, not necessarily correct. Use confidence, p_null, and the intervals to decide what to automate and what to send to review.
  • Dates: Dates without a year are resolved from context. If a field depends on the current date, set reference_date or add a line such as Today: 2026-10-19 to the state.

Pricing

Clairic costs $0.10 per million input tokens. Because it generates no tokens, there is no output token charge.

Get started

Use Clairic through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clairic model page, extraction models, pricing, and the blog post ↗︎.

Oct 19, 2026

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 now available on Workers AI

Workers AI

@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 is now available on Workers AI. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 552B backbone parameters. It activates 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode, which keeps input-heavy agentic workloads fast and low-cost.

The 1017 release is an update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks, and it completes tasks with shorter outputs.

Key capabilities:

  • Vision: Send images alongside text in the same request.
  • Reasoning: Reasoning is on by default at high effort. Set reasoning_effort to low or max to change the effort, or to none to turn reasoning off.
  • Function calling: Build agents that invoke tools and APIs across multiple conversation turns.
  • Long context: A full 1,048,576 token context window.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash requires the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits. The default rate limit is 20 requests per minute with standard Workers AI billing and 50 requests per minute with prepaid AI Gateway credits. For details, refer to limits.

Use DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or AI Gateway.

For more information, refer to the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page and pricing.

Oct 16, 2026

AI Search keyword search supports Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries

AI Search

AI Search keyword search with the trigram tokenizer now matches Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries, including full natural-language questions such as 経費精算の締め日はいつですか？. Previously, a query without spaces was treated as a single exact phrase and usually returned no keyword results.

The porter tokenizer does not work well for these languages. If your content is in Japanese, Chinese, or Korean, set keyword_tokenizer to trigram. Changing the tokenizer triggers a full reindex.

Refer to Keyword search for tokenizer details.

Oct 15, 2026

Pipecat PhoneLLM Mini now available on Workers AI

Workers AIRealtime

@cf/daily-co/phonellm-mini-alpha-2, a model from the Pipecat ↗︎ team at Daily, is now available on Workers AI. PhoneLLM is built for voice agents and other realtime AI applications, where a model has to reply quickly and call the right tool mid-conversation.

In a voice agent, the language model sits between speech-to-text and text-to-speech, so every second it takes adds to the caller's wait. Developers usually choose between a fast model without reasoning mode, which can miss instructions or tool calls, and a slower model in reasoning mode, which handles both well. Pipecat post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 30B on phone and customer support scenarios so PhoneLLM follows instructions and calls tools better without reasoning mode.

You can use PhoneLLM through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. Pipecat recommends temperature: 0. Also set chat_template_kwargs: { enable_thinking: false }.

Run a voice agent with Pipecat on Workers

Pipecat ↗︎ is an open-source Python framework for building voice agents. Now that Python Workers are generally available, you can run a Pipecat voice agent on Cloudflare.

Our Pipecat voice agent example ↗︎ runs in a Durable Object and uses WebRTC as the voice transport through the Realtime SFU. It uses DeepSeek V4 Flash by default. To deploy it with PhoneLLM, give this prompt to your coding agent:

For more information, refer to the PhoneLLM Mini model page, Pipecat's model card ↗︎, and Workers AI pricing.

Oct 13, 2026

Cloudflare API MCP server sends Workers Issues as MCP Events

AgentsWorkers

Workers Issues provides built-in error monitoring for Cloudflare Workers. It detects production failures and groups related failures into issues without an SDK or application wrapper.

The Cloudflare API MCP server now sends these issues as MCP Events ↗︎, the first event it exposes. MCP clients discover cloudflare.alert.workers_observability_real_time_issue with events/list and subscribe with events/subscribe, scoped to an account or a single Worker. When Issues detects a new or recurring issue, the server posts a signed event to the client's webhook, so an agent can start investigating without polling.

To use it, enable Issues on your Worker and connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp with the Notifications Write and Workers Observability Write permissions to a client that supports MCP Events webhooks.

Oct 13, 2026

New persistent browser tool in the Agents SDK, with tabs and logins that last between turns

Agents

The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a browserTool that gives your agent a Browser Run browser it can return to on later turns. Your agent can open a website, inspect a page, and come back to it with its tabs, cookies, and login session intact while the browser session remains alive.

When you give browserTool to your agent, the model writes code that drives the browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Screenshots return as images that an image-capable model can inspect and your UI can display.

To use browserTool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed. Create a Browser, register it with your object's Lifecycle, and add the tool to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

Each Pi conversation gets its own active tab by default. Cookies and logins remain shared within the browser.

The browser stays alive between turns, including when the Durable Object hibernates. Its default idle timeout is 10 minutes. If the session expires or crashes, the tool creates a fresh browser and reports restarted: true. The old tabs and login state are gone.

You can also use the persistent browser with the AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters, or connect another harness through the public Browser and CDP APIs.

Refer to persistent browser tools for the complete Pi Durable example, required bindings, and behavior when a tool call is interrupted.

Oct 12, 2026

New web_fetch tool in the Agents SDK for reading webpages and documents, with automatic markdown conversion

Agents

The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a web_fetch tool that reads webpages, PDFs, and supported Office documents, using Workers AI Markdown Conversion to turn them into text the model can read. The tool requests Markdown directly from sites that support Markdown for Agents and formats JSON for the model.

When you give the web_fetch tool to your agent, the model provides a URL and receives back the page content, along with the final URL, HTTP status, and content type. Long pages come back in smaller sections, with an offset the model can use to continue reading. You control which hosts the agent can fetch, response size, timeouts, and redirects.

When you also provide the web_search tool to your agent, the model is told to use web_fetch to read the pages that web_search returns.

To use the web_fetch tool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed, and add it to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

The web_fetch tool works with any harness. The SDK includes AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters. If you use a different harness, or need to fetch a page without calling a model, use fetchWeb(), windowWebFetchPage(), and renderWebFetchPage() from agents/webfetch. Direct fetching does not require a Durable Object or browser.

For setup, examples, and request controls, refer to Web fetch.

Oct 9, 2026

Clef-omni adds audio and video input, Clef-flash is now cheaper, and Clef is faster

Workers AI

@cf/cloudflare/clef-omni is now available on Workers AI. Clef-omni is a decision model that takes audio (WAV or MP3) and video (MP4 or WebM) input alongside text and images. It joins Clef and Clef-flash in the Clef family of open-weight decision models. We also cut the price of Clef-flash, so it now costs less than Jev, and made Clef faster.

Clef-omni: one decision model for every modality

Previously, making a decision about a voice recording or a video meant chaining models together: transcribe the speech, split the audio and visual tracks, then pass the results to a text decision model. Clef-omni reads every modality directly in one request. A video's soundtrack is aligned with its frames, so the model can reason over what is seen and heard at the same time.

Clef-omni is built on a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) backbone with 3B active parameters. Like the rest of the Clef family, it does not generate text. It scores every allowed answer in a single pass, so decisions return quickly:

  • Text requests: about 20 ms
  • Image or audio inputs: under 100 ms
  • A 21-second video clip with sound: about 300 ms

Pass media as base64 data URLs in the images, audio, and videos fields:

Clef-omni scores highest of the Clef family on BANKING77, CLINC150+OOS, and Amazon ESCI:

Benchmark Clef-omni Clef Clef-flash Jev
BFCL (case exact) 98.2 98.47 98.76 95.75
BANKING77 (macro-F1) 94.8 94.20 90.93 79.74
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) 97.7 97.43 66.77 89.27
Amazon ESCI (macro-F1) 57.8 57.48 57.39 55.21
PhishNChips (accuracy) 73.2 79.60 75.05 62.55

Clef-flash is now cheaper

Clef-flash now costs $0.038 per million input tokens, down from $0.090, which makes it cheaper than Jev. To offer this price, the hosted Clef-flash context window is now 24K tokens, down from 64K. Based on usage data, only 0.24% of requests exceed 24K input tokens. If you need a larger context window, use Clef, which keeps its 64K context window.

The Clef-flash weights on Hugging Face are unchanged and support up to a 256K context window if you self-host.

Model Price Context window
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash $0.038 per M input tokens 24K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef $0.240 per M input tokens 64K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef-omni $0.150 per M input tokens 64K tokens

All Clef models convert image inputs to input tokens, and Clef-omni does the same for audio and video. For details on how each input type is tokenized, refer to the Clef, Clef-flash, and Clef-omni model pages.

Clef is now faster

We optimized how Clef is served on Workers AI, so it now returns decisions up to 2x faster. The model weights are unchanged.

Input size Before: median / p95 (ms) Now: median / p95 (ms) Median speedup
~800 tokens 262 / 438 152 / 351 1.7x
~3,400 tokens 616 / 777 305 / 531 2.0x
~16,000 tokens 2,721 / 3,250 1,635 / 1,805 1.7x

Part of this speedup comes from moving Clef to SGLang ↗︎. Clef support is coming to SGLang in version 0.5.22 (PR #42721 ↗︎). If you self-host Clef, launch commands are available in the Clef collection on Hugging Face ↗︎.

Get started

Clef-omni follows the same System One API as Clef and Clef-flash, and works with AI Gateway. To try it, change the model ID to @cf/cloudflare/clef-omni and set the model selector to clef-omni.

For more information, refer to the Clef-omni model page and pricing.

Oct 8, 2026

AI Gateway log IDs and request IDs now use UUIDv7

AI Gateway

New AI Gateway log IDs and request IDs are lowercase UUIDv7, such as 019a7b3e-5f2c-7c41-9d3e-2b8f6a1c4e07. Previously, log IDs were 26-character ULIDs and request IDs were random UUIDs.

For a request that AI Gateway answers in a single step, the cf-aig-request-id, cf-aig-log-id, and cf-aig-event-id response headers now carry the same value. For provider and Universal requests, if you set your own cf-aig-event-id, AI Gateway returns it instead.

Existing log IDs do not change, and the logs API accepts both formats. Treat log IDs as opaque strings, and update any code that checks for the ULID format.

Standardize provider credential error responses in AI Gateway

AI Gateway

AI Gateway's REST API now returns consistent responses when an AI provider rejects credentials. The change applies to POST /ai/run ↗︎.

Scenario Previous AI Gateway response New AI Gateway response
ElevenLabs Provider-specific UserCredentialsError with HTTP 403 HTTP 401 with error code 2009
Google Vertex HTTP 500 for rejected credentials, with upstream retries HTTP 401 with error code 2009; the request fails without retrying the provider
All other providers HTTP 402 or another provider-specific status for rejected credentials HTTP 401 with error code 2009

Update applications that handle AI Gateway REST API errors to treat HTTP 401 as an invalid or rejected provider credential.

Oct 2, 2026

Run the Pi Durable harness on Cloudflare with the Agents SDK

AgentsWorkers

The Agents SDK now provides first-class support for building agents using the Pi harness. You can build long-running agents using the combination of Pi 1.0 ↗︎, Pi Durable ↗︎, and the new PiHarness class that the Cloudflare Agents SDK provides, ensuring your agent's work is durably persisted, even if interrupted mid-turn.

Built with Earendil ↗︎, this integration is our first step toward first-class support for third-party agent harnesses on Cloudflare.

Beta

PiHarness is in beta. Pi Durable ↗︎ is a new, experimental package, and the PiHarness API will likely change as Pi Durable matures.

PiHarness is a new "Lifecycle capability" provided by the Cloudflare Agents SDK. Pi Durable provides the agent harness and the Lifecycle is responsible for keeping the agent running in the Durable Object. The Lifecycle is a core concept in the Agents SDK ensuring that long-running work can run in a Durable Object, surviving restarts, crashes, and network issues. We will share more on Lifecycle capabilities in the near future.

Install

npm i agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
yarn add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
pnpm add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
bun add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai

Both Pi packages are optional peer dependencies of agents, so you only install them if you use the harness.

Use it in an Agent

Creating a Pi agent requires configuring the Pi Harness with a model, skills, and tools, then registering the PiHarness with the Agent class.

The agents/models/pi-ai entry point supports AI Gateway and Workers AI models, so you can get started with Cloudflare models right away or use your existing Pi AI provider.

Add tools with extensions

Both tools and system prompt sections are provided to the Pi Harness via extensions.

For more information on creating and configuring extensions, refer to Extensions.

Oct 1, 2026

Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI

Workers AI

Meet @cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.

Clef is a decision model, in the same family as Typesafe's Jev ↗︎. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for.

Both models are hosted on Workers AI as Clef and Clef-flash. We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face: Clef ↗︎ and Clef-flash ↗︎. Read the launch blog post ↗︎ for the full story, including how we trained them.

We are also launching a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning service to help you tune Clef for your own workloads. Sign up to work with us as a design partner ↗︎.

Built for the hot path

Clef is designed to be fast so decisions come back in milliseconds. Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster.

Latency Clef Clef-flash Jev
Median 209.3 ms 38.8 ms 524.1 ms
p95 238.6 ms 122.4 ms 536.0 ms

Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users, so the network round trip stays short. You can put Clef directly in the request path of your agent, then hand off to an LLM on Workers AI to take action.

Leading the benchmarks

Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models. A few highlights:

Benchmark Clef Clef-flash Jev
BFCL (case exact) 98.47 98.76 95.75
BANKING77 (macro-F1) 94.20 90.93 79.74
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) 97.43 66.77 89.27
Home appliances (case exact) 82.95 97.73 52.27

On Typesafe's own workflow evals, Clef beats Jev in 3 of 4 areas: invoice processing, customer service, and security incidents. The full results are on the Hugging Face model card ↗︎.

Drop-in compatible with Jev

Model Size Best for Context window
@cf/cloudflare/clef 27B Highest-precision decisions 64K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash 9B Latency-critical, hot-path decisions 64K tokens

Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request, in three types:

  • noul: A yes/no question. Returns the probability that the answer is yes.
  • choice: Pick one option from a set you define. Returns the chosen option, a probability per option, and a confidence value.
  • score: Rate against an ordered rubric. Returns a probability-weighted score and a probability per level.

What you can build with decision models

  • Support triage: Decide whether a ticket is urgent and which team owns it, then route it without a human in the loop.
  • Threat intelligence: Classify a website by category. Paired with Browser Run, Clef fetched, rendered, and classified a domain in 2.2 seconds, compared to 4.7 seconds for gpt-oss-120b in the same workflow.
  • Trust and safety: Score user submissions against your own policy rubric and act on the probability.
  • Agent guardrails: Let an agent check "should I take this action?" in tens of milliseconds before calling a tool.
  • Visual classification: Pass up to four images alongside the state. Unlike text-only decision models, Clef has a vision encoder.

Get started

Use Clef through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clef model page, the Clef-flash model page, and pricing.

Oct 1, 2026

The best way to do MCP auth just got better: Workers OAuth Provider goes v1, with a new split API and full support for MCP 2026-07-28

AgentsWorkers

@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider ↗︎ is now v1, with a new split API. One Worker acts as the authorization server: it signs users in and issues tokens. Your MCP server acts as the resource server, and can run in another Worker. It validates each token with the authorization server over a Service Binding, without crossing the public Internet.

  • It supports the MCP 2026-07-28 authorization specification ↗︎, including Client ID Metadata Documents ↗︎ and issuer identification ↗︎. It still works with older clients, including those using Dynamic Client Registration ↗︎.
  • insufficientScope() gives you step-up authorization ↗︎ in one line.
  • The authorization server and the resource server can run in different Workers ↗︎ with different WAF and rate limiting rules.
  • One authorization server can issue tokens for many MCP servers ↗︎.
  • A migration skill ↗︎ ships in the npm package so a coding agent can perform the upgrade.

The split API

In the example, env.AUTH_SERVER.validateToken is that Service Binding call. The calendar Worker needs no KV namespace of its own.

OAuthResourceServer publishes the RFC 9728 ↗︎ protected resource metadata that MCP clients use to find your authorization server. It answers requests without a token with a 401 challenge that points to that metadata. It also rejects tokens issued for any other resource.

You can still use OAuthProvider as both the authorization server and the MCP server. For most 0.x deployments, the only required change is to add resourceMetadata: { resource }.

Other updates and helpers

  • Consent page ↗︎ and upstream sign-in ↗︎ helpers implement the MCP confused deputy protections.
  • Sliding refresh token expiry ↗︎ with refreshTokenIdleTTL.
  • Resumable KV cleanup ↗︎ with purgeExpiredData().
  • An internal reason ↗︎ on every error passed to onError.

Upgrade with the migration skill

npm i @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
yarn add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
pnpm add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
bun add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest

Point your coding agent at node_modules/@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/skills/migrate-to-1.x/SKILL.md, or follow the migration guide ↗︎.

For both Workers in full, refer to the split Workers example ↗︎.

Oct 1, 2026

AI Search is generally available

AI Search

AI Search is now generally available. Usage-based billing begins on November 1, 2026, with included monthly ingestion, storage, semantic query, and full-text query usage. Cloudflare will send a reminder email the week before billing begins.

Refer to Limits & pricing for rates and included usage.

Hybrid search is on by default

New AI Search instances use hybrid search by default. Hybrid search combines semantic vector retrieval with full-text matching. You can choose a different index method when you create an instance.

Refer to Hybrid search for details.

Workers AI embeddings and reranking are included

Workers AI embedding and reranking calls made by AI Search are included in AI Search pricing. These calls no longer appear on your Workers AI bill or in your AI Gateway logs. Generation, query rewriting, and external providers continue to use your account and gateway.

Refer to Limits & pricing for details.

Multimodal model and image support

AI Search supports the @cf/qwen/qwen3-vl-embedding-2b and google-ai-studio/gemini-embedding-2 multimodal embedding models. Search and chat requests can include images through the REST API and public endpoint.

Refer to Supported models for the full list of embedding models.

OCR availability and increased file limits

Optical character recognition (OCR) is available on every account for scanned PDFs. Plain-text or code files and PDFs with OCR enabled can be up to 10 MiB. PDFs without OCR and other supported formats remain limited to 4 MiB.

Refer to Data source for file limits and Limits & pricing for OCR pricing.

Source type inference

When you create an AI Search instance, the type field is optional. AI Search infers a website source from an HTTP or HTTPS URL, or an R2 source from an existing bucket name.

Refer to Data source for details.

Sep 30, 2026

Sandbox SDK 1.0: control every sandbox from your own Durable Object

Sandboxes

Sandbox SDK 1.0 is available. Your own Durable Object class now controls each sandbox container directly, through the Durable Object container API on this.ctx.container.

With 1.0, your class can:

  • Choose the image and instance size each time it starts a sandbox. One class can run sandboxes on different images, and a deploy does not restart sandboxes that are running.
  • Save the files of a sandbox as a snapshot, in public beta, and start the same sandbox or a new one from it.
  • Decide when each sandbox stops, for example when a task finishes, when its user goes idle, or after it saves a snapshot.
  • Run commands with streamed input and output, send them signals, and open terminals.
  • Serve previews from ports in the sandbox, with your own hostnames and authentication.
  • Handle outbound requests for each hostname in Worker code, so credentials and bindings stay in your Worker.
  • Expose only the methods that you want callers to use.
  • Run an agent in the same Durable Object, and give the model a tool that runs commands in the sandbox.

Your class uses the container API directly, with the durable_object scheduling policy and container snapshots, both in public beta. @cloudflare/sandbox adds classes for work that the API does not include:

  • Files streams files in and out of the running sandbox.
  • S3Mount mounts an S3-compatible bucket, such as R2. Your Worker signs each storage request, so the credentials stay out of the sandbox.
  • DirectoryBackup saves a directory to R2 and restores it into any sandbox, including one on a newer image.

If you use Sandbox SDK 0.x

Your 0.x applications keep running, and @cloudflare/sandbox 0.x stays on npm. Sandbox SDK 0.x receives bug and security fixes until 2026-12-31, and its documentation stays at Sandbox SDK 0.x.

When you are ready, Migrate from Sandbox SDK 0.x shows the 1.0 code for each 0.x feature, including preview URLs, tunnels, background processes, terminals, backups, and the code interpreter. The guide keeps the preview URLs and named tunnels that your 0.x application created working. You can move every sandbox in one deploy, or run a 1.0 class next to your 0.x class and move sandboxes one at a time. The deploy that moves an existing class to the new policy is one-way, so the guide shows how to rehearse it first.

The Sandboxes documentation also covers Dynamic Workers, for untrusted code in JavaScript, Python, or WebAssembly.
